transcript.content: Hello, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Hi, thanks for seeing me. Um… I guess I’ve been having some trouble staying focused, especially with work things. I’m a secondary school teacher, and I’ll sit down with a stack of essays or a curriculum document really intending to get through it, and then after maybe ten minutes I realize I’ve just been staring at the same page. My mind’s gone off in three different directions and I haven’t really taken in what I’m supposed to be reading.  

It’s not that I’m not trying, if that makes sense… it just keeps happening enough that I thought I should probably ask someone about it.
Did you have problems with attention or staying focused when you were a child?

Yes… I think so, though I don’t want to make it sound worse than it was. I did well enough in school overall, but even in primary school my report cards would say things like, um, “bright but careless,” or that I didn’t finish work unless someone was really keeping an eye on me.

And my parents used to find worksheets crumpled up in my backpack that I’d apparently done, or partly done, and just… forgotten to turn in. So, yes, I suppose there were signs back then too, if that’s the sort of thing you mean.
Outside of reading work documents, do you often have trouble finishing everyday tasks once you start them?

Yes… I mean, not with everything, but it does happen more than I’d like. Like if my department chair gives me three or four things to do after a meeting, I’ll usually start the first one and maybe get most of it done, so it’s not that I’m ignoring it.

But then there’ll be some final step — sending the file, or updating the shared calendar, or printing the handouts — and that bit just… doesn’t happen unless someone reminds me. Which is embarrassing, because it’s often a small thing. I know it probably sounds a bit careless.
Do you often find yourself worrying a lot, even when there isn’t a clear reason to?

Um… I wouldn’t say I worry a lot for no reason, no. I mean, I do worry about work things sometimes, like anyone would, but it usually feels tied to something specific.  

I haven’t really noticed myself just feeling anxious out of nowhere, if that’s what you mean. Does that answer it okay?
Have you been feeling down or depressed lately?

Not really, no. I mean, I have off days, and I get frustrated with myself sometimes, especially when work piles up, but I wouldn’t say I’ve been feeling depressed. At least, not in the way I understand it. Is that okay to say?
Do these concentration problems also cause difficulties for you at home?

Yeah… at home too, unfortunately. I’d like to say it’s mostly just a work thing, but it does spill over.

My wife has sort of… taken over a lot of the bills and reminders now, because I don’t always keep track of them reliably. Not because I don’t care, it’s just I’ll mean to do it and then it slips. And at work it’s gotten serious enough that my department chair put me on a support plan because of the missed follow-through.

That feels a bit awful to say out loud, honestly, but yes, it does cause problems at home as well.
Did these concentration problems begin after a specific stressful event or major life change?

No, I don’t think it started after one big event or anything like that.

It’s a little embarrassing, but it goes back pretty far. Even in primary school, my report cards would say things like “bright but careless,” or that I didn’t finish work unless someone was keeping a close eye on me. And my parents used to find worksheets all crumpled up in my backpack that I’d done but just… forgot to turn in.

So, no, I don’t think it was triggered by a stressful change. It’s more like it’s always kind of been there, if that makes sense.
